report.source_text: Renal tissue histology [Figure 3] on light microscopy showed marked mesangial cell increase, some of which contain apoptotic debris; significant features of acute tubular necrosis with simplification of tubular epithelial cells, some of which are cystically dilated containing amorphous eosinophilic material; and interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy in about 10–20% of the section examined. There was no increase in the mesangial matrix and thickening or duplication of the glomerular basement membrane. Features were in keeping with lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old female presented with body swelling, frothy urine, and signs of nephrotic syndrome, renal impairment, and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) activity (leukopenia, anemia, elevated ESR, positive ANA, elevated anti-dsDNA). A kidney biopsy confirmed lupus glomerulonephritis (ISN/RPS Class II), showing mesangial cell increase, apoptotic debris, acute tubular necrosis, and interstitial fibrosis. Treatment included dialysis, intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, and mycophenolate mofetil. After 6 months, there was significant improvement in proteinuria, serum creatinine, eGFR, and ESR. At 10 months, proteinuria, ESR, and hemoglobin remained stable and improved.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with body swelling, frothy urine, facial puffiness, jaw swelling, massive lower limb edema, and ascites.
Initial lab findings included serum creatinine 167.3 umol/l, eGFR 42 ml/min/1.73m2, leukopenia 1.7 × 109/L, anemia 18%, ESR 133 mm/hr, hypoalbuminemia 17.2 g/L, heavy proteinuria 2.7 g/day.
Urine microscopy showed 15–20 pus cells/hpf, numerous dysmorphic red blood cells, granular casts, and epithelial cell casts.
Serological markers included strongly positive serum ANA (homogeneous pattern) and elevated anti-double stranded DNA titer (30 IU/ml).

Kidney biopsy showed marked mesangial cell increase, apoptotic debris, acute tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy, and features consistent with lupus glomerulonephritis (ISN/RPS Class II).
Treatment included dialysis, intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, and mycophenolate mofetil.
After 6 months of treatment, proteinuria reduced to 0.2 g/day, serum creatinine to 94 umol/l, ESR to 44 mm/h, and eGFR rose to 82 ml/min/1.73 m2.
At 10 months, proteinuria was 0.07 mg/day, ESR was 16 mm/h, and hemoglobin concentration was 12 g/dl.

remaining_uncertainties: Status of leukopenia, HDL cholesterol, and triglycerides after treatment
Status of serum ANA and anti-dsDNA titer after treatment
Any documented complications or long-term outcomes beyond 10 months
